title: Stage record files in canonical bytes (file blob == record_blob), so registered rows match the consumer's lookup
objective: Make every rso/slice001/stages/*.json stage record file exactly receipt.canonical_bytes(record), so its committed blob sha256 equals evidence.record_blob(record), the key the consumer's Registry looks up; regenerate the 12 files.
problem: Found by Palamedes preparing T020 (2026-10-04): evidence.Registry registers a stage record iff a STAGE_RECORD row has blob_sha256 == record_blob(record) = sha256(canonical_bytes(record)) (evidence.py ~539). Aporia registered rows 2-19 with blob_sha256 = sha256 of the committed FILE bytes (B5.1/B5.2: the row binds repo_path at commit). The 12 files are not canonical (evidence_plane.py writes json.dumps(indent=2, sort_keys=True) + newline; fire_world.py similar), so for all 12: file hash != record_blob, canonical hash not registered. In the real T020 run every authority would be NO_STAGE_RECORD and every claim UNQUALIFIED. Fix at the writers: emit receipt.canonical_bytes(record) exactly (no trailing newline), regenerate the 12 records (record content unchanged: json.loads(new) == json.loads(old)), and add a test that sha256(file) == record_blob(json.loads(file)) for every stage record. Cadmus's world writer is in owns for this packet (cross-lane, coordinator-authorized).
non_goals: No change to record content, versions or fire receipts
No change to evidence.py lookup semantics
No registration (Palamedes requests re-registration from Aporia)
evidence_required: RED: the new identity test fails on the current 12 files
GREEN: it passes; json content identical to the old files (asserted)

acceptance.condition: every stage record file blob equals its record_blob; content unchanged

history.note: found preparing T020: registry/consumer record-identity mismatch
